problem_text:
A regional power grid operator must inspect eight substations scattered across a service territory.  
The transmission line distances between substations are as follows (in kilometers):
* Substation Alpha to Beta: 174.1 km  
* Alpha to Gamma: 51.3 km  
* Alpha to Delta: 109.3 km  
* Alpha to Epsilon: 183.4 km  
* Alpha to Zeta: 180.7 km  
* Alpha to Eta: 35.1 km  
* Alpha to Theta: 175.4 km  
* Beta to Gamma: 179.8 km  
* Beta to Delta: 64.9 km  
* Beta to Epsilon: 20.8 km  
* Beta to Zeta: 160.0 km  
* Beta to Eta: 196.8 km  
* Beta to Theta: 121.4 km  
* Gamma to Delta: 120.4 km  
* Gamma to Epsilon: 183.5 km  
* Gamma to Zeta: 141.4 km  
* Gamma to Eta: 32.0 km  
* Gamma to Theta: 145.7 km  
* Delta to Epsilon: 76.4 km  
* Delta to Zeta: 148.4 km  
* Delta to Eta: 133.6 km  
* Delta to Theta: 119.6 km  
* Epsilon to Zeta: 147.0 km  
* Epsilon to Eta: 203.3 km  
* Epsilon to Theta: 107.2 km  
* Zeta to Eta: 173.4 km  
* Zeta to Theta: 40.4 km  
* Eta to Theta: 176.1 km  

The inspection team must devise a route that visits every substation precisely once, concluding back at the initial substation, while minimizing the total travel distance along the transmission corridors.
